environment: Mac15,12, Apple M3, 16 GiB unified memory, darwin/arm64, Go 1.26.5
Selected hardware adapter: Apple M3, Metal backend, vendor Apple, driver Metal

observed_result.hardware_test: passed; no GPU test was skipped on this Mac
observed_result.small_case: 3 nodes, 5 declared edges including duplicate, zero, and negative weights; maximum absolute GPU-versus-float32-CPU reference difference 0
observed_result.workgroup_case: 130 nodes and 910 edges crossed two 64-invocation workgroup boundaries; all outputs matched the CPU reference within the test's declared float32 tolerance
observed_result.repeated_execution: same executor reused with new input, source output, and weights; CSR topology transfer measurement remained unchanged
observed_result.validation: invalid topology, input shapes, non-finite values, cancellation, zero-edge execution, and idempotent Close passed

limitations: The timings are host wall-clock observations around API phases, not GPU timestamp-query measurements or a CPU-versus-GPU speedup claim.
This kernel computes only input plus sparse weighted source output in float32. Existing CoImNet dynamics and learning continue to use the CPU float64 reference path.
Sparse backward, device parameter updates, device state save/restore, and Ubuntu RTX 4070 execution have not been verified.

The selected Mac adapter was reported by the library as device_type DiscreteGPU; this record relies on the verified adapter name and Metal backend rather than treating that classification as a hardware specification.
Insyra v0.3.2 exposes dense float32 DeviceMatMul acceleration but no public sparse recurrent device lifecycle; upstream feature request: https://github.com/HazelnutParadise/insyra/issues/379.
